'''Elizabeth Ann Donley''' (born April 5, 1970) is an American physicist. For most of her career, she was a researcher in the Time and Frequency Division at the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), where she served as Chief of the Time and Frequency Division from 2018 to 2025. Donley's research areas have included the operation and development of [[atomic fountain clock]]s and chip scale atomic devices and instruments. In 2025, Donley took early retirement from the U.S. Government and started work as an independent consultant. Now she helps companies develop and use atomic clocks for advanced timekeeping applications.

== Life ==
Donley was born on April 5, 1970.<ref name=":1">{{Cite thesis|title=Single-molecule spectroscopy at subkelvin temperatures|publisher=ETH Zurich|date=2000|degree=Doctoral Thesis|language=en|first=Elizabeth Ann|last=Donley|doi=10.3929/ethz-a-003929922|hdl=20.500.11850/144708 }}</ref> She completed a B.S. in physics from [[University of Nevada, Las Vegas]] in 1994. Donley earned a M.S. in physics at the [[University of Colorado Boulder]] in 1996. Donley completed her doctoral studies in Switzerland, earning a Ph.D. in natural sciences from [[ETH Zurich]] in 2000.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=E.A. Donley |url=https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/author/37265100500 |website=ieee.org |access-date=2019-10-15}}</ref> Her thesis was titled ''Single-molecule spectroscopy at subkelvin temperatures''. Donley's doctoral advisor was [[Urs Wild]].<ref name=":1" /> Her postdoctoral research at the University of Colorado Boulder was on [[Ultracold atom|ultracold atomic physics]] with [[List of Nobel laureates in Physics|2001 Nobel Laureates]] [[Carl Wieman]] and [[Eric Allin Cornell|Eric Cornell]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2" />

Donley joined the [[National Institute of Standards and Technology]] in 2002 as a research physicist in the Time and Frequency Division at the Physical Measurement Laboratory; in 2018 she became its Division Chief.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2">{{Cite journal|url=https://www.nist.gov/people/elizabeth-donley|title=Elizabeth Donley|last=Donley|first=Elizabeth|date=2019-07-30|journal=NIST|language=en|access-date=2019-10-15}}</ref> 

She has served in a number of leadership positions for the [[Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers|IEEE]] professional society, including serving as VP of Frequency Control for the Ultrasonics, Ferroelectrics, and Frequency Control Society in 2018 and 2019 and again starting in 2026.<ref name=":2" /> 

Donley's research areas include the operation and development of atomic fountain clocks and chip scale atomic devices and instruments, for which she has won the [[Department of Commerce Gold Medal]] in 2004 and 2014.<ref name=":0" /> In 2022, she won the IEEE C. B. Sawyer Memorial Award.<ref>{{Cite web |title=IEEE C. B. Sawyer Memorial Award|url=https://ieee-uffc.org/award/c-b-sawyer-memorial-award#recipients |access-date=2023-07-17 |website=IEEE UFFC }}</ref>  In 2024 she won the IEEE Rabi Award.
